observation_summary: The adaptive step size integrator calculates a step size that can exceed the remaining integration range, causing the integrator to evaluate the function outside the intended bounds.
reasoning_summary: The fix introduces a conditional check (if-statement) to validate the calculated step size against the remaining integration range (t). This is a classic boundary check validation error where the logic was missing a guard to ensure the step size does not overshoot the target time.
evidence_used: The fix adds an if-else block checking 'stepStart + stepSize >= t' (or <= t) to truncate the stepSize.
The bug report states: 'this step size is not checked against the integration range, so if the integration range is extremely short, this step size may evaluate the function out of the range'.
The fix is a direct implementation of a missing boundary check.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the step size calculation is part of an algorithm, the specific fix is a guard/boundary check to prevent the algorithm from proceeding with an invalid value, which is the definition of Checking.
